verdict.rationale: OpenCode documents concrete building blocks for background automation: a headless `opencode serve` HTTP/OpenAPI server for programmatic control, a `--auto` flag to auto-approve permissions without human intervention, an SDK for building integrations, and a GitHub integration where OpenCode can autonomously work on an issue in a new branch and submit a PR unattended. However, community evidence flags real caveats — the headless server has no built-in authentication and any local process/webpage can execute code on it (opencode-comm-18), and there's no first-party mention of scheduling/cron-like triggers beyond GitHub events. Missing for 10: independent hands-on confirmation of long-running unattended automations working reliably, documented scheduling/trigger mechanisms beyond GitHub events, and resolution of the unauthenticated-server security gap.
